findings.evidence: "Passengers may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app. Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Replace with content specific to weekend service.

findings.evidence: "Station staff can also help with the same request in person."
findings.fix: Rephrase to clarify staff assistance, such as "Station staff can answer questions about the schedule in person."
findings.violation: The sentence implies staff help patrons "request" to review a schedule, which is awkward; reviewing a schedule is not typically requested.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Replace with content relevant to schedule changes.
findings.violation: This content appears to be duplicated from section 1, paragraph p2, and does not clearly fit in the schedule changes section.

findings.evidence: Steps appear in HTML order as "Confirm your order" (order:3), "Enter payment details" (order:2), "Choose a plan" (order:1)
findings.fix: Reorder HTML elements so they appear in logical sequence without relying on CSS order property.
findings.violation: HTML source order is reversed from the logical/visual order (specified by CSS order property); screen readers will announce steps in wrong sequence.

findings.fix: Add descriptive alt text such as `alt="Delete"`.
findings.violation: Icon image has empty alt text, making it inaccessible to screen reader users.

findings.evidence: Link text reads "read the accessibility improvements list" but href is "/fares/history"
findings.fix: Change link text to match destination, e.g., "read the fare history" or change href to match context.
findings.violation: Link text does not match the destination URL; heading to fare history is not related to accessibility improvements.

findings.evidence: `<label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label>` with no required or aria-required attribute on the input
findings.fix: Add `required` attribute to the phone input and/or `aria-required="true"` to the label.
findings.violation: Red color alone is insufficient to indicate a required field; lacks proper accessibility attributes.

findings.fix: Remove `aria-invalid="true"` or only set it dynamically after validation actually fails.
findings.violation: aria-invalid is set to true on an empty input, indicating a validation error when none has occurred.

findings.fix: Replace "Error." with a specific message such as "Invalid promo code" or "This code has expired".
findings.violation: Error message is too generic and does not explain what is wrong with the promo code.
